title: Hilbert's 5th Problem: the Exponential Bridge from Lie Algebra to Lie Group
description: Answers the second open question of the parent entry hilbert-5: extend the formalization with actual Lie-algebra infrastructure from Mathlib to state the exponential-map properties. The parent states the Gleason–Montgomery–Zippin solution of Hilbert's 5th problem at the level of axiomatized deep theorems (out of reach of present-day Mathlib); this entry instead formalizes, fully verified, the genuine algebraic/analytic content that sits underneath the Lie correspondence: the Lie bracket of an associative algebra (⁅X,Y⁆ = X·Y − Y·X, from Mathlib.Algebra.Lie.OfAssociative) and the exponential map of a real Banach algebra (NormedSpace.exp ℝ, from Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Algebra.Exponential). The exponential map is the concrete bridge from the Lie algebra to the Lie group: an algebra element X is an infinitesimal generator and t ↦ exp(t·X) is the one-parameter subgroup it generates. The file proves the bracket vanishes iff the generators commute, that exp(X+Y) = exp X · exp Y when ⁅X,Y⁆ = 0, and the one-parameter-subgroup homomorphism laws (γ(0)=1, γ(s+t)=γ(s)·γ(t), γ(−t)·γ(t)=1, and that the image is abelian). 8 theorems, 1 definition, 0 sorries, 0 axioms, no native_decide.

mathlibDependencies.description: The exponential map exp ℝ : 𝔸 → 𝔸 of a real Banach algebra, with exp 0 = 1 and (for commuting x, y) exp(x+y) = exp x · exp y. Supplies the analytic content of the one-parameter subgroup t ↦ exp(t·X).

On an associative ring the Lie bracket is the commutator ⁅x,y⁆ = x·y − y·x. Used to translate bracket-vanishing into commutativity, the link between the Lie algebra structure and the multiplicativity of the exponential.
Scalar multiples of a fixed element commute: from Commute X X one gets Commute (s·X) (t·X). Supplies the commutativity hypothesis for exp_add_of_commute in the one-parameter-subgroup addition law.

overview.historicalContext: Hilbert's 5th problem (1900) asks whether a continuous (merely topological) group of transformations must carry a differentiable structure — whether Lie's theory survives dropping the differentiability assumption. It was resolved affirmatively for locally Euclidean groups by Gleason, Montgomery, and Zippin (1952), after von Neumann's 1933 compact case. The technical heart of Lie theory, in any of its forms, is the exponential map exp: 𝔤 → G from the Lie algebra to the Lie group, which converts the (linear) bracket structure of 𝔤 into the (nonlinear) multiplication of G and supplies the one-parameter subgroups that recover the smooth structure.
overview.problemStatement:
**Open Question (hilbert-5 OQ-02)**: Can the formalization be extended with actual Lie algebra infrastructure from Mathlib to state the exponential map properties?

**Formalized**: Using Mathlib's Lie bracket on an associative algebra and its Banach-algebra exponential, this entry states and verifies the exponential-map properties that underlie the Lie correspondence — bracket-vanishing ⇔ commutativity, multiplicativity of exp on commuting generators, and the full one-parameter-subgroup homomorphism laws for γ_X(t) = exp(t·X).
overview.text: A 127-line formalization in 8 theorems and 1 definition, parametric in a real Banach algebra 𝔸. Section 1 (the Lie bracket): commute_of_lie_eq_zero, lie_eq_zero_of_commute, and lie_eq_zero_iff_commute establish ⁅X,Y⁆ = 0 ↔ Commute X Y from Mathlib's of_associative_ring_bracket and sub_eq_zero. Section 2 (multiplicativity): exp_add_of_lie_eq_zero derives exp(X+Y) = exp X · exp Y from a vanishing bracket via exp_add_of_commute. Section 3 (one-parameter subgroup): oneParam X t := exp ℝ (t·X), with oneParam_zero (exp_zero), oneParam_add (add_smul + commutativity of scalar multiples + exp_add_of_commute), oneParam_neg_mul (the additive inverse of time gives a multiplicative inverse), and oneParam_commute (the image is abelian). All compile with 0 sorries, 0 axioms, no native_decide.
overview.proofStrategy:
**Bracket ⇔ commute**: LieRing.of_associative_ring_bracket rewrites ⁅X,Y⁆ to X·Y − Y·X; sub_eq_zero turns vanishing into X·Y = Y·X, which is definitionally Commute X Y.

**Multiplicativity**: feed commute_of_lie_eq_zero into NormedSpace.exp_add_of_commute (valid in a real Banach algebra since ℝ is RCLike and 𝔸 is a complete normed algebra).

**One-parameter subgroup**: oneParam_zero is exp_zero after 0•X = 0; oneParam_add rewrites (s+t)•X = s•X + t•X (add_smul), proves Commute (s•X) (t•X) by ((Commute.refl X).smul_left s).smul_right t, and applies exp_add_of_commute; oneParam_neg_mul uses oneParam_add backwards with neg_add_cancel and oneParam_zero; oneParam_commute uses oneParam_add and add_comm.
keyInsights: **The exponential map is the bridge**: an algebra element X is an infinitesimal generator (a tangent vector at the identity of the Lie algebra), and t ↦ exp(t·X) is the one-parameter subgroup of the group it generates. This is the concrete object Hilbert's 5th problem is ultimately about — the smooth structure latent in a continuous group.

**Bracket vanishing is commutativity**: in the associative model the Lie bracket is the commutator, so ⁅X,Y⁆ = 0 ⇔ X·Y = Y·X. This is the exact hypothesis under which the exponential is multiplicative.

**Abelian infinitesimally ⇒ abelian after exponentiation**: exp(X+Y) = exp X · exp Y precisely when ⁅X,Y⁆ = 0 — the verified, finite-dimensional shadow of 'an abelian Lie subalgebra integrates to an abelian subgroup'.

**One-parameter subgroups are genuine homomorphisms (ℝ,+) → (𝔸,×)**: γ(0)=1, γ(s+t)=γ(s)·γ(t), γ(−t)·γ(t)=1, and the image is abelian — the homomorphism laws follow from the additivity of t ↦ t·X and multiplicativity of exp on commuting elements.

**Reuse of real Mathlib infrastructure**: unlike the parent entry, which axiomatizes the deep Gleason–Montgomery–Zippin theorems, this entry uses only fully-proved Mathlib lemmas (NormedSpace.exp and the associative-algebra Lie bracket), so every statement is kernel-checked with 0 axioms.

**Generality**: the results hold in any real Banach algebra, including matrices and bounded operators over ℝ — exactly the matrix Lie group setting where the exponential map is the matrix exponential.

conclusion.summary: Answers the second open question of hilbert-5 by extending the formalization with genuine Mathlib Lie-algebra and exponential infrastructure. It states and verifies the exponential-map properties at the heart of the Lie correspondence: the associative Lie bracket vanishes iff its generators commute (lie_eq_zero_iff_commute); the exponential is multiplicative on commuting generators (exp_add_of_lie_eq_zero); and the one-parameter subgroup oneParam X t = exp(t·X) obeys the homomorphism laws making it a one-parameter subgroup with abelian image. 8 theorems, 1 definition, 0 sorries, 0 axioms, no native_decide, parametric in any real Banach algebra.
conclusion.implications: Where the parent entry can only axiomatize the deep solution of Hilbert's 5th problem, this entry shows that the concrete machinery the solution rests on — the exponential bridge from Lie algebra to Lie group — is already verifiable in Mathlib today, with no axioms. It gives a clean, reusable kernel for any future formalization that needs one-parameter subgroups or the exp(X+Y) = exp X · exp Y identity.

mainTheorems.name: oneParam_add
mainTheorems.statement: For an infinitesimal generator $X$ in a real Banach algebra, the one-parameter subgroup $\gamma_X(t) = \exp(tX)$ satisfies $\gamma_X(s+t) = \gamma_X(s)\,\gamma_X(t)$.
mainTheorems.significance: The defining homomorphism law of a one-parameter subgroup and the headline 'exponential map property' the open question asks to state. Proved from additivity of $t \mapsto tX$ and multiplicativity of $\exp$ on the commuting elements $sX$ and $tX$.
mainTheorems.description: γ_X(s+t) = γ_X(s)·γ_X(t): the one-parameter subgroup is a homomorphism (ℝ,+) → (𝔸,×).

mainTheorems.name: exp_add_of_lie_eq_zero
mainTheorems.statement: If $\lbrack X, Y\rbrack = 0$ in a real Banach algebra then $\exp(X+Y) = \exp X \cdot \exp Y$.
mainTheorems.significance: Connects the Lie bracket directly to multiplicativity of the exponential — the verified shadow of 'an abelian Lie subalgebra integrates to an abelian subgroup', and the exact statement the parent's Lie-correspondence narrative needs.
mainTheorems.description: Vanishing Lie bracket ⇒ exp is multiplicative on X, Y.

mainTheorems.name: lie_eq_zero_iff_commute
mainTheorems.statement: $\lbrack X, Y\rbrack = 0 \iff X$ and $Y$ commute, in any associative algebra.
mainTheorems.significance: The algebraic hinge: the associative-algebra Lie bracket is the commutator, so its vanishing is exactly commutativity — the hypothesis under which the exponential is multiplicative.
mainTheorems.description: Bracket vanishes iff the generators commute.
